_comment: AI Engine Optimization rules. AEO is distinct from SEO — optimizing for citation by Perplexity, ChatGPT, Claude, and Gemini, not just Google ranking.

quickAnswer.position: top of page, before any other content
rules: Must lead with a specific number ($, %, x, or count)
Must be self-contained — an AI engine should be able to cite just this block
No hedging (avoid: 'it remains to be seen', 'only time will tell')
Must answer the query directly, not introduce the article
quickAnswer.example: $347B in exits in Q1 alone — more than all of the previous year combined. The exit window is wider than it has been since 2021, and late-stage companies are rushing to capitalize before rates shift again.

factualDensity.note: A paragraph with 5 data points gets cited 3-5x more often than one with 5 opinions.

rules: Every claim must be attributable to a specific source, person, or organization
At least one named entity per section
No anonymous claims ('experts say', 'some believe', 'industry insiders')
Link entities to their canonical identifiers when possible (sameAs URLs)
Break into clear H2/H3 sections — each section answers one specific question
Use descriptive headings (questions work well for AEO)
Add 'Key Takeaways' bullet list (3-5 items, each starting with a number)
Tables and lists are more extractable than prose paragraphs

schemaRequirements.note: Dataset schema surfaces pages in Google Dataset Search — an underused traffic channel that 95% of competitors ignore.

measurementMetrics.description: Percentage of your top queries where your domain appears in AI search results
Average data points per 1K words across site content
Percentage of content pages with a quick-answer block at top
